sections.h2: How does property tax work for a house in Caldwell County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Caldwell County property tax is assessed by the county Property Valuation Administrator and collected by the Caldwell County Sheriff, with unpaid bills moving to the county clerk after April 15. The assessment date is January 1, and the PVA values most real estate at fair cash value, with every parcel physically reviewed at least once every four years, according to the Kentucky Department of Revenue.

Princeton is the county seat, and the county covers about 345 square miles of land in the Western Kentucky Pennyrile. Most of what a seller in Caldwell County sees on a bill is the sum of several taxing districts: the state, the county, the school system and any special districts. Each district sets its own rate, and the PVA does not set rates or collect money.

The county has long been farm country. The Kentucky Department of Revenue notes that farmland is assessed at its agricultural value, and the Caldwell sheriff's site explains that a parcel of ten or more acres used for livestock or crops, including timber, can qualify for that treatment. A seller with acreage should ask the PVA whether the land is carried at agricultural value before listing, because a buyer can lose that status if the use changes.

sections.h2: What are the Caldwell County tax payment dates and penalties?
sections.html:
Caldwell County bills become payable on November 1, with a 2% discount through November 30, face amount in December, a 5% penalty in January, and a 21% penalty from February 1 through April 15. The sheriff's office states this schedule on its tax page, and it matches the statewide framework in KRS 134.015.

The 2026 collection began November 2, 2026, with bills mailed October 30, and the sheriff switched from postcards to letter-style bills this year. A payment counts for a phase if it is postmarked, paid at the office or dropped in the box before the next phase starts. Here is how the phases line up:

  • November: 2% discount off the bill.
  • December: face amount, no discount and no penalty.
  • January: 5% penalty added.
  • February 1 to April 15: 21% penalty added.

Payment options at the sheriff's office on the first floor of the courthouse in Princeton include check, money order, cashier's check, cash, and credit cards in the office, which carry a processor convenience fee. The drop box sits on the east side of the courthouse beside the door, and cash must not go in it. The sheriff's own page lists office hours of 8 am to 4 pm, Monday through Friday, and the office closes for state holidays.

sections.h2: Who do I call in Caldwell County about a bill, a value or a delinquent tax?
sections.html:
Call the sheriff at 270-365-2088 about a bill, the PVA at 270-365-7227 about a value or exemption, and the county clerk at 270-365-6754 about delinquent bills. The PVA works from the courthouse at 100 East Market Street, second floor, and the sheriff's mailing address is 100 E. Market St., Room 25, Princeton.

  • Sheriff: sends bills, takes payments through April 15, and posts a bill search on its website that is for viewing only.
  • PVA: assesses property, processes homestead and disability applications, and sets up the conference you need before any appeal.
  • County clerk: collects delinquent bills after April 15 and records deeds.

A bill goes to the owner of record on January 1. If you bought during the year and the seller got the bill, ask them to forward it, or print a copy from the sheriff's site. The sheriff does not see new deeds, so a buyer's name often appears in care-of form first.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Caldwell County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the PVA office, then file with the county clerk within one workday after the public inspection period ends. The tax roll opens for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May, and the local board of assessment appeals meets for up to five days starting 25 to 35 days after that, per the state property tax calendar.

Bring facts, not opinions. The board expects physical details of the land and buildings, insurance records, construction cost and comparable sale listings, and it denies appeals that arrive without them. If you skip the local board, you lose the right to carry the appeal to the next level. A seller who thinks a Caldwell County value is too high should also remember that if bills print before an appeal ends, your own stated opinion of value is used, and a supplemental bill follows if the final number comes out higher.

After the roll closes, the value on the bill is the number the buyer's lender and title company will see. A seller in Princeton with an old home that has had a roof or addition done should check that the PVA's record of the house matches what is actually there.

sections.h2: What relief programs reduce Caldwell County property tax?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption applies to owner-occupants who are 65 or older or totally disabled, and it reduces the assessed value rather than the bill itself. The sheriff's page gives the maximum as $46,350 for 2024 and 2025 and says the amount is adjusted every two years under KRS 132.810, so ask the PVA for the current figure.

To qualify, you must own and live in the property, show proof of age, and not claim an exemption anywhere else. Applications are completed at the PVA office, and Caldwell's sheriff says it takes less than five minutes. The state explains that the exemption follows the owner, not the house, so a buyer from you must apply on their own.

A seller who is 65 or older should confirm the exemption was on this year's bill before closing. If it was missing, the PVA can correct it, and the sheriff asks owners to settle that before paying.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when I sell a Caldwell County house?
sections.html:
The tax lien stays with the property, and the closing agent usually prorates the year between you and the buyer. The Caldwell sheriff's FAQ says your agent or lender should explain how the bill is prorated and paid, because the sheriff's office is not told about those arrangements.

Unpaid bills do not disappear at closing. After April 15, delinquent bills pass to the county clerk with added penalties and 1% monthly interest, according to the Department of Revenue's collection process page. If you are selling a Princeton house with back taxes, ask the clerk for the payoff amount before setting a closing date.

If the loan servicer escrows taxes, the bill still comes to the owner, and the sheriff says it is the owner's job to forward it. Check with the servicer a few times a year so a missed forward does not turn into a penalty.

sections.h2: What should I know about Caldwell County and Princeton before selling?
sections.html:
Caldwell County has about 12,600 residents and a housing market priced well below northern Kentucky, with a median owner-occupied home value of $118,500 in the 2020 to 2024 Census estimates. Princeton, population 6,270 in 2020, grew around railroad junctions and is home to the University of Kentucky Research and Education Center, a Bremner cracker plant is among the county's larger employers, and a 2021 tornado damaged homes in the southern part of town.

Sellers with repairs, tenants or a damaged roof often choose a direct cash sale to skip showings and repair bargaining.

faqs.q: When is Caldwell County property tax due?
faqs.a: Bills are payable from November 1, and the 2% discount runs through November 30. December is the face amount, January adds 5%, and February 1 through April 15 adds 21%. After April 15 the sheriff transfers unpaid bills to the county clerk.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Princeton?
faqs.a: Pay at the Caldwell County Sheriff's Office on the first floor of the courthouse, by mail to 100 E. Market St., Room 25, or in the east-side drop box. The website bill search is for viewing only, and the office does not take payments by phone.

faqs.q: Can I get an exemption if I am over 65 in Caldwell County?
faqs.a: Yes, if you own the home, live in it and are 65 or older this year. Apply in person at the PVA office with proof of age. The exemption reduces the assessed value and must be reapplied for by a new owner.

faqs.q: What if I sell a Caldwell County house before the bill arrives?
faqs.a: The bill goes to the owner of record on January 1, so the seller may still receive it. The closing agent prorates the year, and the buyer should print the bill from the sheriff's site if it never arrives.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix my house to sell it in Caldwell County?
faqs.a: No. Kentucky does not require repairs before a sale, and a cash buyer can purchase as-is. Back taxes and liens still have to be paid from the proceeds, so get the amounts from the sheriff or clerk early.
